title: A repeat node draws its children once for each value of an index
body:
Today the only repetition is `repeat N` on `line` and `arrow`, which draws N copies and moves each named cell index on by one per copy. Nothing else repeats. A figure with four thread quarters, four braces, four strips and four arrows writes each one out, or comes from a script. The sufr pipeline figure in `sufr-figures` comes from a Python script partly for this reason, and its 110 gather arrows and 111 slots are each a line of the script's output.

## Proposal

A node `repeat NAME FIRST LAST { ... }` draws its children once for each whole number from FIRST to LAST. In each copy, NAME stands for that number wherever a `let` name can appear, so it works inside `(…)` arithmetic.

```text
repeat i 0 3 {
    box { at (x0 + i * w) y; size w 24; fill tint; }
    arrow { from (x0 + i * w + w / 2) (y + 28); to (x0 + i * w + w / 2) (y + 70); }
}
```

`scene/expand.rs` already substitutes `let` names before `scene` reads a node, so the copies can be made there and `scene` sees plain nodes.

## Open

- How a copy picks the i-th of several values, such as the four thread colours. One option is `let tints a b c d;` with `(tints i)` choosing one.
- A named child inside a `repeat` is defined once per copy. Either each name gets the index appended, or a named node inside `repeat` is an error.
- What a drag in acre-gui rewrites for a node that `repeat` made. acre-4518a5 records the same question for computed values.
